According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple is preparing several new features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 that should be more appealing to health-conscious users. The company is also testing two new case finishes for the rumored ceramic version.

New Health Feature Upgrades

If you're dissatisfied with the Apple Watch as a fitness tracker, these two major health feature upgrades should get your attention. They are all-day heart rate tracking and a completely redesigned app that makes it easier to extract valuable insights from your health data. Here's Gurman's description of the new app:

As a current WHOOP user, I have to say the main thing that has always appealed to me is how the WHOOP app makes it easier to learn from my health data. It shows me all the factors that contributed to a poor night of sleep or recovery, but with the Apple Watch, it feels like the only thing that matters is the Activity rings. If Apple makes real progress here, I'll be very happy.

The key to a richer data experience with the Apple Watch is having more data. Apple is reportedly testing keeping the heart rate sensor recording continuously throughout the day, rather than only during workouts or at random intervals.

Two New Case Finishes

We've previously heard that Apple is considering a ceramic material for the Apple Watch Series 12, and Gurman now reports there will be two color options: a traditional white and a dark gray. There will also be "a lot of new band colors and configurations."

A Future Redesign

The current Apple Watch design language, introduced with the Apple Watch Series 10 in 2024, was a relatively modest change that made the watch thinner but sacrificed the screen bezels. According to Bloomberg, we could see a full Apple Watch redesign with next year's Series 13, though it might be pushed back to the Series 14:

I'm very curious to see what Apple comes up with here. It seems like they've hit a ceiling with the rounded design language, so maybe we'll see a completely new look. Hopefully it won't affect compatibility with old bands.
